name: WALDO
shortDescription: Voice-controlled pan/tilt flashlight turret: person detection and keyword spotting run as ExecuTorch models on the two NPUs of one Alif E8 board. No PC, no cloud.
description:
WALDO patrols a room, spots people with its camera, points its flashlight at them and keeps following, and you steer it by voice. Everything runs on a single Alif Ensemble E8 DevKit.

Highlights:
- Sees: YOLOv8n (28 room classes, 320 × 320) running entirely on the Ethos-U85 NPU.
- Hears: a fine-tuned MicroNet-M keyword spotter (10 command words) running entirely on the Ethos-U55 NPU.
- Two brains, one chip: always-on audio on the M55-HE core, vision and control on the M55-HP core, talking through a shared mailbox in SRAM.
- One state machine (PARKED → SENTRY → TRACK → HOLD) with a Kalman-style tracker; the servos run on hardware timer PWM at 50 Hz with no CPU cost.
- An ESP32-S3 camera head streams colour JPEG over UART at about 28 fps.
- CI runs both models on Arm's Corstone FVP simulators on every push.
- The turret is parametric OpenSCAD: board box, fork and head, with flashlight and laser sleeves.

A team build for the Arm × Meta ExecuTorch hackathon (October 2026).
